title: Student Transportation Services Bus Pass Rules: First Pass, Replacements and Free Replacement Credits
content:
**Rule.** Every Student Transportation Services rider receives a bus pass when service starts, charged the first-pass fee of the pass schedule. A lost or damaged pass is replaced on request with a new pass number, and each replacement posts the replacement pass fee. The first replacements of the school year on the assignment, up to the type's number of free replacements, are credited in full as free replacements on the day they post; later replacements are owed. A pass that stops working through no damage is exchanged as a replacement and its fee credited in full the same way. Replacement fees are not waived by meal status and do not count toward the household permit fee cap.

The count is of the replacement passes issued on the assignment in the school year before the pass being issued.

## Decision table

| Replacement passes already issued on the assignment this school year | Type's free replacements per year | The new replacement |
|---|---|---|
| fewer than the free number | 2 | fee posts and is credited in full the same day |
| equal to or more than the free number | 2 | fee posts and is owed |
| any | 0 | fee posts and is owed |

## Examples (hypothetical)

- A McKinney-Vento School-of-Origin Transportation rider loses a pass for the first time this school year: the 5.00 USD replacement fee posts and is credited in full the same day. A third replacement that year is owed.
- A Courtesy Rider Permit (Annual) rider's pass is damaged: the 5.00 USD fee is owed. The fee is not waived for a student holding a Free Meal Status tier, and it does not count toward the household cap.
